title: Exception Case Standards: Supporting Statement, Decision Clock and Single Decision (Formulary Benefit)
content:
## Case standards

**S1. Statement before approval.** An exception request under the Formulary Benefit is decided only on a prescriber supporting statement. No request may be approved before a statement for it has been received. This is read from the request's case history.

**S2. Who may open a request.** A request may be opened by:
- the prescriber;
- the member, where the member's Northbridge formulary allows member-initiated requests;
- an authorized representative, who must have an appointment-of-representative form on file where the formulary requires one.

Where the formulary takes intake around the clock, expedited requests are accepted at any hour.

**S3. Decision clock.** The decision clock starts at the event that the formulary names as its clock start. A standard request is decided within the formulary's standard decision hours and an expedited request within its expedited decision hours. A prescriber's expedited attestation on the statement makes the request expedited.

**S4. Missing statement.** When no statement has arrived by the end of the formulary's statement wait (a number of calendar days after the request was received, with the request date as day zero), the request is denied as *missing prescriber statement*. That denial may be recorded only after the full wait of calendar days has elapsed since the request was received.

**S5. One decision per request.** A request that has already been approved, denied or withdrawn takes no further decision. A new request starts a new case.

## The missing-statement clock in detail

- **Starting event:** the moment the request was received, as shown on the request in the member's exception history.
- **Counting:** calendar days, with the request date as day zero.
- **Comparison:** the denial date must fall after the last day of the wait. The last day of the wait itself does not satisfy the condition, because that day has not fully elapsed.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, on a formulary with a 10-day wait).* A request is received on 1 March (day zero). Day 10 is 11 March.
- A missing-statement denial dated 11 March is not permitted, because day 10 has not fully elapsed.
- A missing-statement denial dated 12 March is permitted, provided no statement has arrived.

On a formulary with a 14-day wait, the same request reaches day 14 on 15 March, and the earliest permitted denial date is 16 March.

## Q&A on the standards

*Can a request be approved on the strength of the member's own account of the prescriber's opinion?* No. Approval needs a prescriber supporting statement received for that request.

*A request was denied for a missing statement, and the statement then arrives. Is the denied request reopened?* No. A decided request takes no further decision, and a new request starts a new case.
